newsitem.title: USA: Charter One withdraws Standard Federal bid.
newsitem.headline: Charter One withdraws Standard Federal bid.

text.p: Charter One Financial Inc said on Tuesday it has withdrawn its proposal to merge with Standard Federal Bancorporation Inc, determining the deal was "economically unfeasible."

Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV agreed to buy Standard Federal for $1.95 billion and its executives said earlier that they were not concerned about Charter One's bid, which was $47 million higher than its own.
Charter One, which has about $14 billion in assets with 172 branches in Ohio and Michigan, said its decision was made after a review of the merger agreement between Standard Federal and ABN AMRO.
Standard Federal operates 182 branches in Michigan, Ohio, Illinois and Indiana with assets of $15.5 billion.
